# ADR-FIN-001 — FIN's SEC/MDL dependencies are not modeled as XM rows except one SOFT-READ

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P2 (Database)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
`srs-fin.md` §A8 carried forward, from `module-registry-fin.md` (P0), three "HARD-FK"
rows against SEC (User; ModuleRegistry/ScreenRegistry/ActionRegistry) and one "HARD-FK"
row against MDL (LookupType/LookupValue). At P2, assigning the actual `XM-*` register
from these candidates surfaces a discrepancy: `shared/XM-PROTOCOL.md` and this factory's
own knowledge base (`erp-domain-standards.md §5`) define `HARD-FK` as "a physical foreign
key to another module's table." No such physical, cross-module foreign key exists
anywhere in this pipeline — not in SEC's own script (its own audit columns are a
"principal string, not a numeric FK" by its own explicit db-script rule), not in MDL's
(its one cross-module dependency, XM-MDL-001, is SOFT-READ, and its own self-registration
into SEC was never modeled as an XM at all).

## Decision
P2 assigns exactly one XM row, `XM-FIN-001` (SOFT-READ → MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE), covering
every FIN column backed by one of FIN's 13 owned-but-MDL-hosted lookup keys. FIN's
dependency on SEC for identity and authorization (every request, via the same CORE
interceptor pattern SEC's and MDL's own P3.1 plans already describe) and FIN's own
self-registration into SEC (module/screens/actions, via SEC's REST onboarding endpoints)
are **not** given `XM` rows — they are narrated as platform-standard integration in
FIN's own P3.1 backend execution plan (Phase 1 CORE and Phase 7 SEC-BE), exactly
mirroring how SEC's and MDL's own P3.1 plans already handled the identical pattern.

## Consequences
- No SRS content changes — `srs-fin.md` §A8's three SEC rows remain readable as the
  *functional* dependency statement they always were (FIN cannot operate without SEC);
  this ADR only corrects which of them becomes a formal, P2-owned `XM-*` record.
- `db-script-fin.md` carries no cross-module physical FK anywhere, consistent with every
  other module built so far.
- A future reviewer comparing `srs-fin.md` §A8 ("HARD-FK") against `db-script-fin.md` §2
  (one SOFT-READ XM, the SEC rows absent) should read this ADR as the reconciling record,
  not a defect.

## Traces
ENT-FIN-001, ENT-FIN-004, ENT-FIN-007, ENT-FIN-008, ENT-FIN-009, ENT-FIN-010,
ENT-FIN-011, ENT-FIN-013 · REQ-FIN-001, REQ-FIN-007, REQ-FIN-008, REQ-FIN-010,
REQ-FIN-014, REQ-FIN-018, REQ-FIN-022, REQ-FIN-025, REQ-FIN-031, REQ-FIN-044,
REQ-FIN-045 · XM-FIN-001

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-002.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-002 — the api-docs input carries an API ID BINDING annex, and the backend registry's API range is stale

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
`_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` is generated from the implemented backend's OpenAPI document and
emits no governance `API-*` id — it knows verbs, paths and DTOs, nothing about the factory's
id grammar. Two contracts read that file expecting ids in it: C8.2/C8.3 (the api-docs and
`registry-exec-be` must name the same API ids) and C9.5 (every `API-*` the frontend plan
cites must be defined in the api-docs).

Two facts about the surface:

1. The published surface is exactly 37 endpoints, and `backend-execution-plan-fin.md`
   defines exactly `API-FIN-001 .. API-FIN-037`. Matched on verb + path the mapping is 1:1
   with no shape diff — every planned verb and path is the published verb and path.
2. `registry-exec-be-fin.md` still reads `API-FIN-001 .. API-FIN-032`. The five endpoints
   added after that registry was last written — API-FIN-033 (fiscal-period search),
   API-FIN-034, API-FIN-035, API-FIN-036, API-FIN-037 (the four deactivates) — are in the
   backend plan and in the SRS Part B tables, but never reached the registry. `gov.py
   analyze` already reports this against P3.1 as five C7.4 findings.

## Decision
An **API ID BINDING** annex is added to `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md`, following the precedent of
`_inputs/api-docs-sec.md` (ADR-SEC-004): one row per `API-FIN-*`, binding it to the endpoint
this document publishes, matched on verb and path. No endpoint is invented, no id is
re-numbered, and the generated body below the annex is untouched.

The annex binds all 37, including 033–037. The frontend is planned against the surface that
exists, not against a registry line that has fallen behind it.

## Consequences
- C9.5 resolves: every `API-FIN-*` the frontend plan cites is now defined in the api-docs.
- C8.3 resolves in the registry→artifact direction: all 32 registered ids are in the annex.
- C8.2 will report five findings in the artifact→registry direction — API-FIN-033..037 are
  in the api-docs and absent from `registry-exec-be`. Those findings are **true**, and their
  fix is one line in the backend registry's ID RANGES, which is P3.1's artifact and outside
  this stage's boundary (§8: P3.2 references `API`, never writes a backend artifact). They
  are recorded here rather than hidden by binding only the first 32 — binding 32 would have
  made the checker quiet and the plan wrong about the surface it is written against.
- No `REQ-*` changes and no operation is added or removed by this decision.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-003.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-003 — container pattern for the five report screens, which have no entry sub-view

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
§A.4's container-pattern decision order is written for entry screens: it chooses between
`TREE_MASTER_DETAIL`, `FULL_PAGE` and `SIDE_DRAWER` by the shape of the data a user edits.
Five FIN screens edit nothing at all — SCR-FIN-008 (account ledger), SCR-FIN-009 (trial
balance), SCR-FIN-010 (balance sheet), SCR-FIN-011 (income statement) and SCR-FIN-012
(dimension reports). Each is a read-only report: the SRS marks their B3 "not applicable" and
their B1 "single screen (report; no entry)", and each is served by exactly one `GET` endpoint
(API-FIN-028, API-FIN-029, API-FIN-030, API-FIN-031, API-FIN-032). Running the decision order
over them asks which pattern hosts a form that does not exist.

## Decision
A screen with no entry sub-view carries `FULL_PAGE`, stated as
`FULL_PAGE (no entry sub-view — ADR-FIN-003)`, and no fourth pattern is invented. The three
`SIDE_DRAWER` / `TREE_MASTER_DETAIL` / `FULL_PAGE` values stay exactly as §A.4 defines them
for the seven screens that do have an entry.

## Consequences
- The five report screens each get one route and one lazy chunk, with no `new`, `:id` or
  `:id/edit` route and no drawer.
- Their filter state is mirrored into the route's search params so a filtered report is
  linkable — the drill-down chain REQ-FIN-046 asks for (statement line → trial balance →
  account ledger → entry) is navigation between screens, and each hop must be addressable.
- Nothing about the entry screens' patterns changes, and no `REQ-*` is affected.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-004.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-004 — lookup values are read through the lookup module's consumer API, and each such field mints a UXD

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
`profiles/erp.yaml → conventions.lookups` requires every LOV value to be runtime-loaded from
the lookup module, with no hardcoded enum in an API or a field spec. FIN owns 13 lookup keys
(`srs-fin.md` §A6) and registers all of them into MDL as data (REQ-FIN-045); it stores only
codes and keeps no display text of its own (`erp-domain-standards.md` §2.3).

`_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` publishes no lookup endpoint. It cannot: the values live in MDL,
and the endpoint that serves them is MDL's own consumer read, `API-MDL-011`
(`GET /api/v1/mdl/lookups`, query param `type` = the lookup key; response
`List<LookupValueResponse>`, active values only, ordered by `sortOrder`, `nameAr`/`nameEn` per
value — `backend-execution-plan-mdl.md` → API-MDL-011), which is a gated endpoint of another
module, not of FIN.

Twelve of the 13 keys are actually displayed on a FIN screen. `PAYMENT_METHOD` is registered
by REQ-FIN-045 but no FIN column or field cites it in this version, so no screen shows it.

## Decision
Every FIN field whose displayed label comes from a lookup value is a cross-module display
dependency in §A.5's sense — a screen this module owns, showing data whose authoritative
source is another module's real API — and mints a `UXD-*`. One `UXD-*` per lookup key, not
per screen occurrence: the key is the unit the single shared hook is built on, and minting
the same dependency twelve times over for twelve screens would record the same fact twelve
times.

`UXD-FIN-001 .. UXD-FIN-012` are minted accordingly, one per displayed key, each naming the
screens that display it and each resolving through API-MDL-011.

The cross-module endpoint is named in `ui-ux-spec-fin.md`, where the `UXD-*` are defined.
`frontend-execution-plan-fin.md` cites the `UXD-*` and never the foreign path or the foreign
API id: C9.5 requires every `API-*` cited in that plan to be defined in FIN's own api-docs,
and a foreign module's id is by construction not.

## Consequences
- One shared hook per key, long-lived cache, shared across every screen that shows the key;
  a lookup field is a `string` holding the code everywhere in the models, and no enum and no
  union of literals is modelled anywhere in the plan.
- `LOOKUP_VALID` validators bind to the runtime-loaded option list, never to a static list.
- If MDL has not seeded a key, its select renders empty and the field stays a required code
  the user cannot satisfy — a deployment-data condition (REQ-FIN-045 onboarding), not a
  frontend fallback. No default value is invented client-side.
- `ACCOUNTING_EVENT_TYPE` is host-defined and seeded with zero values (§A6); its select is
  legitimately empty until a host registers event types.
- No `REQ-*` changes.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-005.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-005 — screen gating reads the security module's effective menu; FIN publishes no permission-read endpoint

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
§RF4 requires every route element to be guarded by its permission, and §RF5 requires a
navigation guard per screen. The names are fixed and not in dispute: the SRS Access summary
and `backend-execution-plan-fin.md` declare `PERM_FIN_ACCOUNTS_VIEW`, `PERM_FIN_RULES_UPDATE`,
`PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE` and the rest, all following
`PERM_<PAGE_CODE>_<ACTION>`.

What no FIN endpoint publishes is the *caller's own* set. `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` has no
endpoint returning the current principal's permissions or screens — every FIN endpoint is a
business operation gated by `@PreAuthorize`, and REQ-FIN-044 states the design deliberately:
FIN registers its module, screens and actions **into the Security module** and owns no
security of its own [POL-FIN-015]. The caller's effective grants are therefore SEC's to
serve, through the effective-menu read its own frontend plan already binds
(`registry-exec-be-sec.md` → API-SEC-027).

## Decision
A FIN screen's navigation guard is "this screen's page code is present in the effective menu
the security module serves for this caller" — the same gate SEC's own screens use. FIN
neither publishes nor duplicates a permission read, and composes no permission name at
runtime.

Action-level affordances (create, update, run, reverse, close-approve) render for a caller
who holds the screen, and the server's `FIN-403-FORBIDDEN` is the authority on the write
itself, shown as its localized catalog message. A second client-side test would be a weaker
copy of the server's.

As with ADR-FIN-004, the foreign endpoint is named in `ui-ux-spec-fin.md`; the execution plan
states the gate in terms of the page code and never cites a foreign `API-*` id.

## Consequences
- Every route of a FIN screen carries that screen's VIEW gate, including `new`, `:id` and
  `:id/edit` — the gateway convention (`conventions.security_model.gateway_action`) means no
  other permission applies without VIEW anyway.
- `PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE` (RULE-FIN-015) is not readable client-side either, so the
  hard-close and year-end-close affordances render for any caller holding `FIN_PERIODS`, and
  a caller without the approval permission receives the server's 403. The separation of duty
  is enforced where the rule says it is — in the Security module — not by hiding a button.
- A failure to load the menu renders no FIN entry and grants no FIN route: access narrows,
  never widens.
- No `REQ-*` changes; RULE-FIN-015 is unaffected.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-006.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-006 — operations the SRS names for which no endpoint is published are omitted, not faked

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
`srs-fin.md` Part B names several operations that `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` publishes no
endpoint for. The SRS itself records each one and why, at the §B4 of the screen that owns it;
this ADR is the frontend's single place of record for the set:

| Operation | Screen | SRS record |
|---|---|---|
| update a recurring/reversing template | SCR-FIN-004 | §B4 "OPEN DEFECT — `update` (template) is still missing" |
| update an allocation rule | SCR-FIN-005 | §B4 "OPEN DEFECT — `update` (rule) is still missing" |
| read one account / template / allocation rule / fiscal year / fiscal period by id | SCR-FIN-001, 004, 005, 007 | §B4/§B5 "deliberate v1 exclusion" — the search result already carries the full record |
| delete a rule line, a template line, an allocation target | SCR-FIN-003, 004, 005 | §B4 "FIN publishes no `DELETE` endpoint on any screen" |
| deactivate the parent Dimension | SCR-FIN-002 | §B4 "deliberately has no deactivate" |

Two of these are recorded by the SRS as real gaps (template update, allocation-rule update);
the rest are reasoned v1 exclusions. Either way the frontend faces the same question.

## Decision
No affordance is drawn for an operation with no published endpoint. A screen shows what it
can really do: a template or an allocation rule created with wrong content can be retired
(API-FIN-036, API-FIN-037) and not corrected, and the screen says so in its empty-state and
row affordances rather than offering an Edit that would have nowhere to go.

Where a by-id read is absent, the entry hydrates from the row the search query already holds
in cache — the search responses of API-FIN-001, API-FIN-012 and API-FIN-015 carry the full
record, lines and targets included, so no second read is needed and an invalidation re-reads
through the same key. SCR-FIN-006 is the exception and reads by id (API-FIN-022), because a
journal entry's lines are what REQ-FIN-016 and REQ-FIN-027 need and the search result is the
place they would otherwise have to come from.

The fiscal-year search was published on 2026-09-19 (API-FIN-038). The discovery workaround this
ADR accepted is retired: it yielded ids and no displayable attribute, which is why SCR-FIN-007's
Master pane and the required `fiscalYearId` inputs of API-FIN-030/031 could not be driven by a
user. **By-id read on a fiscal year remains a deliberate v1 exclusion** — unchanged, and for the
reason already stated: the search row carries every field a by-id read would.

## Consequences
- The operations coverage table in the plan's ALIGN-FE section carries a `✗` row with this
  ADR for each omitted operation — a `✗` for a missing endpoint, never for a missing decision.
- If a template-update or rule-update endpoint is later published, the screen gains an Edit
  affordance and this ADR is superseded for that row; no other part of the plan changes.
- No `REQ-*` is unmet by the omission: none of the six operations is required by a `REQ-*`
  (the SRS states this per screen), which is why each is non-breaking.

> **Narrowed by ADR-FIN-065 (2026-09-24):** "no by-id read" holds for endpoints only. SCR-FIN-002, 003, 004, 005 and 007 are list + `/new` + `/:id` record pages whose cold deep link hydrates through the published search filtered by `<entity>Pk EQUALS id` (page 0, size 1); no by-id endpoint is invented.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-007.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-007 — API-FIN-020 (build an entry from an accounting event) is bound but drawn on no screen

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
`POST /api/v1/fin/journal-entries/from-event` (API-FIN-020) takes an `EventEntryBuildRequest`
— `eventReference`, `eventTypeCode`, `docDate`, `baseAmount`, and free-form `amounts` and
`fields` maps — and builds, validates and posts an entry through the event-type rule
(REQ-FIN-010..013). `srs-fin.md` SCR-REQ-FIN-006 §B5 lists it as "build event entry
(system)", and US-FIN-004 is written from the accounting engine's point of view, not a
user's: "As the accounting engine, I need to build a balanced entry from an incoming
canonical event". §A2 puts the host's business module, the event consumer and the transport
layer explicitly out of scope.

The caller is therefore another system, over the platform's in-process module interface —
not an accountant with a form. A screen that let a user type an `eventReference` and an
amounts map would be inventing a data-entry path for a payload whose whole purpose is that it
arrives from a host.

## Decision
API-FIN-020 is **bound** — it has an F2 block on SCR-FIN-006 stating its verb, path, request,
response and error routing, so the surface is completely accounted for — and is **called by
no screen**. Its entries are seen in the journal-entry list like any other source, keyed by
`journalTypeCode = EVENT_GENERATED` and carrying an `eventReference`; the drill-down of
REQ-FIN-046 ends on exactly that field.

## Consequences
- The operations coverage table carries API-FIN-020 with a `✗` route and this ADR.
- REQ-FIN-010..013 remain covered by the frontend in the only way a UI can cover them: the
  entries the engine builds are searchable, readable line by line, and reversible, on
  SCR-FIN-006.
- No `REQ-*` is left without a screen: the traceability matrix maps US-FIN-004 to
  SCR-REQ-FIN-006, which is exactly where those entries are seen.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-008.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-008 — `journalTypeCode` is a required input on the manual-entry form, although SRS B3 marks it system-set

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context
`srs-fin.md` SCR-REQ-FIN-006 §B3 reads: "Header fields: docDate, periodId, descriptionAr,
descriptionEn (ENT-FIN-004; docNo/statusCode/journalTypeCode system-set)".

The published `JournalEntryCreateRequest` (API-FIN-019) declares four required header fields:
`docDate`, `fiscalYearId`, `periodId` and **`journalTypeCode`** (maxLength 20), plus the
optional descriptions and the required `lines[]`. So the request carries two fields B3 does
not list as inputs: `fiscalYearId` and `journalTypeCode`. `docNo` and `statusCode` are indeed
absent from the request and are system-set exactly as B3 says.

`fiscalYearId` is not in dispute — RULE-FIN-017, added during SVC-API, requires the submitted
period to belong to the submitted fiscal year and the document date to fall inside that
period, which means all three must be submitted together for the rule to have anything to
check.

`journalTypeCode` is the real divergence. ENT-FIN-004 declares it required and lookup-backed
(`JOURNAL_TYPE`: EVENT_GENERATED, MANUAL, RECURRING, ALLOCATION, REVERSAL), and for a manual
entry there is exactly one value the SRS admits: `MANUAL` (REQ-FIN-014, POL-FIN-018 — a manual
entry follows the same path as any other source, classified by its source).

## Decision
The manual-entry form submits `journalTypeCode = MANUAL` as a **fixed, non-editable value**,
rendered read-only beside the header rather than offered as a select. The field is in the
form model because the request requires it; it is not an input because the screen has exactly
one legitimate value for it and the SRS says so.

`fiscalYearId` is a real input, selected together with the period: the period select is filtered
by the chosen year, and RULE-FIN-017 is the server-side check behind that pairing.

## Consequences
- No `JOURNAL_TYPE` select appears on the entry form; the key is still displayed (read-only,
  and on the search filter it is a real select) and still resolves through UXD-FIN-005.
- A user cannot mislabel a manual entry as `EVENT_GENERATED` or `REVERSAL` — those values are
  produced by API-FIN-020 and API-FIN-021 respectively, never by this form.
- The SRS B3 line stays accurate about `docNo` and `statusCode` and is narrowed, here and in
  `ui-ux-spec-fin.md` → SCR-FIN-006, for `journalTypeCode` and `fiscalYearId`.
- No `REQ-*` changes and no rule is weakened: RULE-FIN-017's three fields all reach the server.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-009.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-009 — Test-generation derives from the ACs alone: the frontend denominator, the uncovered as-built paths, and the two ACs with no endpoint

Module  : FIN     Version : v1     Stage raised : test-gen (Test Generation, standalone)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)

## Context

The test-gen engine derives one `TC-*` per `AC-*` and forbids questions, so three ambiguities in
FIN v1 had to be settled here rather than asked about. All three arise from the same fact: FIN's
as-built artifacts describe more behaviour than its forty-six acceptance criteria state.

**(a) Not every AC can be exercised by a screen.** The coverage rule is that every `AC-FIN-*`
carries ≥1 TC, and each track's plan reports its own `AC covered n/total`. Six ACs have no screen
at all: AC-FIN-010 … AC-FIN-013 are event-driven, and API-FIN-020 is bound but drawn on no form
(ADR-FIN-007); AC-FIN-044 and AC-FIN-045 are deployment-time onboarding, which the P0.5
traceability matrix itself records as "— (onboarding, no screen)". Reading the frontend
denominator as 46 would mark six permanent ✗ gaps and block a run that has no defect in it.

**(b) FIN ships behaviour no AC, REQ or RULE states.** The `FIN-409-NOT-ACTIVE` run gate on
API-FIN-014 / API-FIN-017 was closed on a recorded human decision and the Error Catalog says so in
its own RULE column; API-FIN-033 (fiscal-period search), API-FIN-034 … API-FIN-037 (the four
deactivates), the keying-id 404s on the three report endpoints and the dormant-year lineless
closing entry are all as-built additions or narrowings. A test-generation engine that wrote TCs
for them would be inventing the acceptance criteria it claims to derive from — and the FIN
artifacts warn twice, in as many words, that a later session "must not cite `FIN-409-NOT-ACTIVE`
as pre-existing spec".

**(c) Two ACs name no endpoint.** §3 rule 4 requires every backend TC to cite the `API-*` it
exercises. AC-FIN-044 and AC-FIN-045 are satisfied by onboarding and by migrations, and FIN
publishes no endpoint for either.

## Decision

1. **The frontend track's denominator is the ACs a screen can exercise — 40 of 46.** The six
   outside it are listed in the frontend plan's header, each beside the backend `TC-*` that does
   cover it, and the coverage block states the module-wide figure of 46/46 alongside the in-track
   40/40. They are recorded as out-of-track, never as ✗. The backend track's denominator stays the
   full 46, and covers all of them.

2. **No TC is written for behaviour no AC states.** Those paths are cited only where an AC's own
   Given needs them as setup: API-FIN-035 is the only way AC-FIN-021's inactive dimension value is
   reachable, and API-FIN-034 is one of two ways AC-FIN-013's ruleless event type is reached. Both
   test plans carry an explicit "catalog rows no TC exercises" list naming every such code, so the
   absence is legible rather than silent. `FIN-403-SOD-VIOLATION` is treated differently again: it
   is not merely uncovered but **struck**, and TC-FIN-038 asserts the permission gate while
   explicitly asserting nothing about global user-set disjointness.

3. **AC-FIN-044 and AC-FIN-045 get a TC with an empty `Exercises` binding**, reading
   "— deployment-time onboarding; FIN publishes no endpoint for it", rather than being bound to a
   foreign module's endpoint or skipped. Their `traces=` carries the AC and the REQ, which is what
   the contract requires; the `API-*` half of §3 rule 4 has nothing to cite.

4. **Where an AC's REQ maps to several endpoints, the TC binds to the one the AC's own When
   describes**, and names the others only when the AC's Then reaches them — AC-FIN-003 exercises
   API-FIN-004 and then API-FIN-019, because its Then says "REQ-FIN-019 subsequently rejects any
   posting to it".

## Consequences

- `AC covered` reads 40/40 on the frontend track and 46/46 on the backend track; no ✗ appears in
  either, and the module-wide claim of 46/46 is true rather than arithmetic sleight of hand.
- `API covered` reads 26/37 on the backend track. The eleven endpoints without a TC are each named
  in the API → TC index with their reason. That number is expected to stay below 37 until a
  requirement exists for the as-built additions; a later reader should not treat it as a defect in
  this plan.
- Nothing in FIN changes: no REQ, AC, RULE, API, screen or catalog row is added, removed or
  reworded by this decision. It records what the test plans do and do not claim.
- The honest gap this exposes is upstream, not here: `FIN-409-NOT-ACTIVE`, RULE-FIN-017's two 400s
  and the deactivate endpoints are delivered behaviour with no acceptance criterion. Writing those
  ACs is a P1 act; until then this engine cannot cover them without fabricating requirements.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-010.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-010 — DIRECT account derivation is removed outright, not deprecated or restricted; dimension values use their own source list (constant or business field)
Status      : RESOLVED-IN-DIALOGUE
Stage       : P0        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : analysis-dialogue · round 3 · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-09-23T09:50:31+00:00
Dialogue-key: c5212de91644
traces      : POL-FIN-014, POL-FIN-020, POL-FIN-021, POL-FIN-022, POL-FIN-026

## Decision
Accepted from round 1 (option A); round 2 agreed. DIRECT is the only way an account code could come in through the event payload. That breaks domain-profile G6, POL-FIN-014, POL-FIN-020 and v1's own rule "Account numbers in event payloads — never", so v1 never had a legitimate use for it. Deprecating it would protect nothing: v1 was never delivered (project-registry pipeline status: "deliver BLOCKED"), so no configuration data uses DIRECT. Restricting it would leave one value that is allowed for dimensions but forbidden for accounts, and every later stage would have to handle that ambiguity. `ACCOUNT_DERIVATION_TYPE` keeps CONSTANT and MAPPING only, and dimensions use `FIN_DIMENSION_VALUE_SOURCE`. Sources: change manifest §1; domain-profile G6, G1.
traces: POL-FIN-021, POL-FIN-022, POL-FIN-026

Source      : governance-shared/analysis/modules/FIN/v2/_state/briefs/P0-round3.response3.md

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-FIN-011 — A dimension value that a rule line declares, if missing from the event or failing validation, rejects the event and nothing is posted
Status      : RESOLVED-IN-DIALOGUE
Stage       : P0        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : analysis-dialogue · round 3 · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-09-23T09:50:31+00:00
Dialogue-key: 4727e93a6e36
traces      : POL-FIN-024, POL-FIN-027, POL-FIN-028

## Decision
Accepted, and upgraded from a recommendation to CONFIRMED. The request text requires it: §2 says "same discipline as accounts" and "existing validation is not bypassed", and §1 says "never a default, never a guess". Posting the line without the dimension would produce entries with no branch, which is exactly the parallel-run mismatch this change set is meant to prevent. A rule line that declares no dimension still produces a line without one, the same as a manual line. Sources: change manifest §1, §2, acceptance 4.

# ADR-FIN-014 — One distinct, catalogued period-not-open code covers every existing period whose state refuses posting; a date with no defined period is a configuration error, not this code
Status      : RESOLVED-IN-DIALOGUE

Status      : RESOLVED-IN-DIALOGUE

Round 1's recommendation A was conditional on whether FIN v1 had already claimed US ids. It has: `governance-shared/analysis/modules/FIN/v2/_state/current-prd.md` (the stage's own artifact, which delta mode requires this stage to consult for numbering) holds FIN v1's US-FIN-001…019. Drafting this delta at 001 would silently redefine 14 of those ids — exactly what `analyze.py`'s `ids-continue` check exists to catch, and a direct violation of the SEQUENCE RULE ("never reused"). I renumbered the whole draft to **US-FIN-020…033** and re-ran `gov.py analyze -m FIN -v 2`: no `ids-continue` finding, no C4 finding beyond the expected "gate not yet approved". I did not read any v1 story content — only the id count — to keep this dialogue's reasoning independent of borrowed scope.

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-023.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-023 — A MAPPING rule line names its business field in a dedicated lookup-backed field; the derivation value is the constant account code only

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P1 (SRS)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : REQ-FIN-049, REQ-FIN-050, RULE-FIN-019, ENT-FIN-010, US-FIN-021, US-FIN-022

## Context
In v1, `RuleLine.accountDerivationValue` (ENT-FIN-010) is one free-text field whose meaning depends
on `accountDerivationTypeCode`: an account code for CONSTANT, an event field name for DIRECT, a
"mapping-set key" for MAPPING. v2 removes DIRECT (ADR-FIN-010) and makes MAPPING real. Under
MAPPING the line has to name the business field whose value in the event selects the account
(payment method, expense type code). Those names come from the FIN-owned lookup
`FIN_EVENT_BUSINESS_FIELD` (ADR-FIN-013). The profile rule is that a lookup-backed value lives in
a field bound to a lookup key and never in free text. The current overloaded text field breaks
that rule for MAPPING.

## Decision
ENT-FIN-010 gains `accountBusinessFieldCode`, a lookup field on `FIN_EVENT_BUSINESS_FIELD`. It is
required when the derivation type is MAPPING and empty when it is CONSTANT.
`accountDerivationValue` is narrowed to the constant account code. It is required when the type is
CONSTANT and empty when it is MAPPING. RULE-FIN-019 enforces both pairings. The "mapping-set key"
reading of v1 is dropped. The mapping store's key is (the rule's event type, the line's business
field, the event's value for that field), so there is no set to name.

## Consequences
- P2 adds one lookup-backed column to the rule-line table, and XM-FIN-001's key count grows with
  the new lookup type. P3.1 adds the field to the add-rule-line request.
- No v1 data is affected: no rule line was ever built with MAPPING, because v1 answered it with an
  unsupported error.
- Override: to keep a single field, store the `FIN_EVENT_BUSINESS_FIELD` code in
  `accountDerivationValue` and validate it against the lookup when the type is MAPPING.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-024.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-024 — An account mapping references its account by id, and its key is fixed once created

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P1 (SRS)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : ENT-FIN-015, REQ-FIN-054, REQ-FIN-056, REQ-FIN-060, RULE-FIN-023, US-FIN-025

## Context
The change manifest (§1) describes each mapping entry as holding "the account code it resolves to".
It leaves two choices open. The first is whether the entry stores the account's code as text or a
reference to the Account entity (ENT-FIN-001). The second is which fields an administrator can
change after the entry is created. US-FIN-025 asks for mappings to be added, changed and
deactivated.

## Decision
1. `AccountMapping.accountId` is a reference to ENT-FIN-001. The mapping screen displays the
   account's code and names from the Account itself. A text code would duplicate the chart of
   accounts (ARCH-2), and a typo would not surface until an event failed to post.
2. The mapping's key is `eventTypeCode`, `businessFieldCode` and `businessValue`. The key is fixed
   once the mapping is created. A change (REQ-FIN-056) replaces the account only. To move a mapping
   to another key, deactivate it and create a new one. A key edited in place would silently
   redirect a business value that other lines rely on. Deactivate-and-create leaves both rows in the
   audit trail, and RULE-FIN-022 (one active mapping per key) needs no update-time variant.
3. Deactivation is soft (`isActiveFl`) [KB:erp-domain-standards §6], and there is no reactivation.
   A deactivated key is restored by creating a new mapping, which RULE-FIN-022 allows because the
   old row is inactive.

## Consequences
- The update request carries `accountId` alone. P3.1 publishes no key edit.
- RULE-FIN-023 validates the referenced account (active leaf) when a mapping is saved. RULE-FIN-007
  still validates it at post time, because the account can be deactivated after the mapping is
  saved (REQ-FIN-052).
- Override: allow a key edit on update and add an update-time uniqueness check to RULE-FIN-022.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-025.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-025 — Dimension tags are submitted with their rule line and follow its lifecycle

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P1 (SRS)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : ENT-FIN-016, REQ-FIN-062, SCR-REQ-FIN-003, US-FIN-026

## Context
US-FIN-026 needs a rule line to carry dimension values derived from the event (RuleLineDimension,
ENT-FIN-016). The stories say how a tag is declared and how it is resolved. No story says how a
tag is changed or removed afterwards. In v1 the rule line itself (ENT-FIN-010) is add-only. The
as-built record at SCR-REQ-FIN-003 §B4 lists no update and no delete for a line, and FIN publishes
no `DELETE` endpoint on any screen.

## Decision
A rule line's dimension tags are part of the same submission that adds the line (REQ-FIN-062). They
are created and read with the line and are never edited or deleted on their own. This follows the
v1 lifecycle of the rule line exactly. A separately managed tag would be the only independently
editable child of an add-only parent.

## Consequences
- No new endpoint and no new permission are needed. The tags travel inside the existing add-rule-line
  operation, which `PERM_FIN_RULES_UPDATE` gates (SCR-REQ-FIN-003 §B4).
- Inherited limitation, stated rather than hidden: a line tagged wrongly can only be retired by
  deactivating its rule. The v1 note on SCR-REQ-FIN-003 §B4 says deactivation does not free the
  event type for a replacement rule. That limitation is v1's, is unchanged here, and is recorded
  as a known gap.
- `crud-covered` reports ENT-FIN-016 as having no update or delete requirement. That is expected
  under this decision.
- Override: publish add-tag and remove-tag operations on an existing rule line, gated by
  `PERM_FIN_RULES_UPDATE`, together with an update and delete REQ for ENT-FIN-016.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-026.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-026 — A business-field dimension value resolves by code within the tagged dimension

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P1 (SRS)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : REQ-FIN-063, REQ-FIN-069, RULE-FIN-027, ENT-FIN-003, ENT-FIN-016, US-FIN-026, US-FIN-028

## Context
When a dimension tag's source is BUSINESS_FIELD, the event carries a text value, for example the
branch code `BR-07`. The journal line needs a DimensionValue (ENT-FIN-003). ADR-FIN-012 defers any
translation table between legacy codes and FIN values. That leaves one decision open: how the
event's text becomes a FIN dimension value.

## Decision
The event's value resolves to the DimensionValue of the tagged dimension whose `code` equals it.
The comparison is exact. `DimensionValue.code` is unique within its dimension (RULE-FIN-002), so at
most one row can match. No match means the value cannot be resolved (RULE-FIN-027, REQ-FIN-069),
and the event is rejected (POL-FIN-028). The system never falls back to a default, and it never
matches on a name. A match that is inactive is rejected by the existing dimension check
(RULE-FIN-009, REQ-FIN-067).

## Consequences
- For the parallel run, FIN's organisation and branch dimension values need to carry the legacy
  codes as their `code`. That is migration data and outside this version. If the codes turn out to
  differ, the deferred US-FIN-033 is the activation path.
- The lookup has to find a DimensionValue by (dimension, code), and P2 needs an index on that pair.
- Override: case-insensitive matching, or the deferred translation table (US-FIN-033).

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-027.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-027 — Error identities for the v2 rejections: four new distinct errors, two v1 codes confirmed unchanged

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P1 (SRS)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : REQ-FIN-051, REQ-FIN-053, REQ-FIN-068, REQ-FIN-069, REQ-FIN-072, REQ-FIN-073, REQ-FIN-074, REQ-FIN-075, RULE-FIN-004, RULE-FIN-008, RULE-FIN-020, RULE-FIN-021, RULE-FIN-027, RULE-FIN-028, US-FIN-024, US-FIN-030, US-FIN-031

## Context
The change manifest says FIN's analysis owns the name of the dedicated unmapped-value error (§1). It
also asks to "confirm" that a non-open period has its own catalogued code, and to add one only if
none exists (§4). The consumer branches on these answers: a duplicate is acknowledged, a closed
period waits and retries, and every other rejection fails. So each rejection has to be
distinguishable from the others. Error-code strings are catalogued by P3.1. What this stage settles
is which rejections are distinct errors.

## Decision
1. **Confirmed unchanged (US-FIN-030, US-FIN-031).** The v1 catalogue already carries
   `FIN-409-DUPLICATE-EVENT` (RULE-FIN-004) and `FIN-409-PERIOD-NOT-OPEN` (RULE-FIN-008). Each is
   distinct from every validation and configuration error. Consumers will depend on these strings,
   so they are kept verbatim. v2 changes only when they are raised. A uniqueness refusal from the
   store answers the duplicate error too (RULE-FIN-004, as modified). The period-not-open answer
   covers every existing period whose state is not Open (ADR-FIN-014).
2. **Four new distinct errors.** Each gets its own code in FIN's existing `FIN-{status}-{NAME}`
   house style, named by P3.1:
   - unmapped business value (RULE-FIN-020): configuration gap. The fix is to add a mapping.
   - missing business field (RULE-FIN-021): payload gap. The fix is at the producer.
   - unresolvable dimension value (RULE-FIN-027): a value with no FIN dimension value.
   - no defined period for the event's date (RULE-FIN-028): calendar setup. Per ADR-FIN-014 this is
     never the period-not-open code.
   These rejections are kept apart because each is fixed by a different party, and a consumer or
   operator reading only the code has to know which fix applies.
3. **Retired.** The v1 code for "MAPPING is unsupported" no longer has a cause. MAPPING is now
   implemented (REQ-FIN-050), and DIRECT is gone (ADR-FIN-010). P3.1 retires the code from the
   catalogue, and no v2 requirement raises it.

## Consequences
- P3.1 catalogues the four new codes, each with the ar/en message of its RULE. It documents
  `FIN-409-PERIOD-NOT-OPEN` as the retryable rejection for the consumer (REQ-FIN-075).
- Override: fold the missing-business-field case into the unmapped-value error if one
  configuration signal is preferred. The distinctness of the period-not-open and duplicate answers
  is required by POL-FIN-030 and POL-FIN-031 and cannot be overridden.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-028.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-028 — Physical shape of the v2 mapping store, dimension tags and lookup changes

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P2 (Database)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : ENT-FIN-010, ENT-FIN-015, ENT-FIN-016, REQ-FIN-045, REQ-FIN-049, REQ-FIN-050, REQ-FIN-054, REQ-FIN-055, REQ-FIN-059, REQ-FIN-062, REQ-FIN-064, REQ-FIN-065, REQ-FIN-072, RULE-FIN-004, RULE-FIN-019, RULE-FIN-022, RULE-FIN-025, RULE-FIN-026, DBF-FIN-041, DBF-FIN-101, DBF-FIN-102, DBF-FIN-148, DBF-FIN-152, XM-FIN-001

## Context
The v2 SRS (CS-FIN-001) adds two entities (AccountMapping, RuleLineDimension), one RuleLine field
(`accountBusinessFieldCode`), and changes to four FIN-owned lookup keys. It fixes the fields and
rules. It does not fix these structural points, which P2 has to settle:

1. Table names for the two new entities.
2. Lengths for the new code columns and for `businessValue`. The SRS gives only "lookup" and "text".
3. Whether RULE-FIN-019 and RULE-FIN-026 (the derivation spec or tag matches its source) become
   database CHECKs. v1's DEFAULT keeps every lookup value set out of local CHECK constraints.
4. How RULE-FIN-022 ("one ACTIVE mapping per key") becomes a constraint. A plain UNIQUE would
   also block a replacement row once the old one is deactivated.
5. How the v2 lookup changes reach MDL. The engine (§4.2) requires a seed block against the owning
   module's table for every key this module owns. v1 left all 13 keys to FIN's onboarding through
   MDL's API (REQ-FIN-045).
6. Whether existing `FIN_RULE_LINE` rows need converting now that DIRECT is gone and
   `account_derivation_value` is only the constant account code.

## Decision
1. **Names.** `FIN_ACCOUNT_MAPPING` (ENT-FIN-015) and `FIN_RULE_LINE_DIM` (ENT-FIN-016), following
   v1's `FIN_JOURNAL_LINE_DIM`. Columns use the script's one transformation (camelCase to
   snake_case), so the PK is `rule_line_dimension_pk`. This is the transformation the header
   states. v1's `journal_line_dim_pk` is an applied name and stays as it is.
2. **Lengths.** Every new column that stores an MDL lookup code is `VARCHAR(50)`, the width of
   `MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE.code`, so any code MDL accepts fits. `business_value` is `VARCHAR(100)`, the
   width v1 gave `event_reference`, the other host-supplied code. It holds a host code as-is, or
   a PAYMENT_METHOD code (≤ 50) when the field is PAYMENT_METHOD.
3. **Exclusive-or CHECKs that name no lookup code.** `CHK_FIN_RULE_LINE_DERIVATION_SPEC` requires
   exactly one of `account_derivation_value` and `account_business_field_code` to be non-null.
   `CHK_FIN_RULE_LINE_DIM_VALUE_SPEC` does the same for `dimension_value_id` and
   `business_field_code`. Which one each type needs (CONSTANT → value, MAPPING / BUSINESS_FIELD →
   field) stays in the application layer, validated against MDL (XM-FIN-001). The v1 DEFAULT
   holds: no local CHECK lists a lookup code. Every existing v1 rule line satisfies the new CHECK:
   its value is NOT NULL and the new column is NULL.
4. **Partial unique index.** `UQ_FIN_ACCOUNT_MAPPING_ACTIVE_KEY` is UNIQUE on (event_type_code,
   business_field_code, business_value) WHERE is_active_fl. It follows the v1 precedent
   `UQ_FIN_ACCOUNT_RETAINED_EARNINGS` and lives in BLOCK 7. A deactivated mapping keeps its row,
   which is the soft-delete default, and does not block a new active mapping for the same key.
   RULE-FIN-025 is a plain `UQ_FIN_RULE_LINE_DIM_LINE_DIM` UNIQUE (rule_line_id, dimension_id). A
   tag has no active flag.
5. **Seed block against MDL, idempotent.** BLOCK 8 writes the v2 lookup changes into
   `MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE` / `MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE`, which MDL owns. It inserts 2 types, their 6 values and
   PAYMENT_METHOD's CHEQUE. It also deactivates ACCOUNT_DERIVATION_TYPE's DIRECT, a soft retire, so
   AC-FIN-045's "exactly 2 active values" holds and the id is not destroyed. Every statement is
   guarded by `NOT EXISTS` on MDL's own unique keys (`UQ_MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE_KEY`,
   `UQ_MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE_TYPE_CODE`), so it can run before or after FIN's API onboarding
   (REQ-FIN-045), in either order, any number of times. The 11 unchanged v1 keys are not
   re-seeded. This is a migration.
6. **No data conversion.** ADR-FIN-010 records that no data ever used DIRECT, since v1 never
   delivered it. MAPPING raised "unsupported" in v1, so no v1 rule line can depend on it. The
   migration only relaxes `account_derivation_value` to NULL-able and adds the new column.

## Consequences
- P3.1 validates the per-type pairing (RULE-FIN-019, RULE-FIN-026), tag-value-belongs-to-dimension
  (RULE-FIN-026) and PAYMENT_METHOD membership (RULE-FIN-024) in the application layer. The database
  guarantees only the exclusive-or and the uniqueness.
- P3.1 maps a unique violation on `UQ_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRY_EVENT_REF` to the duplicate-event error
  (RULE-FIN-004 as modified; REQ-FIN-072). The constraint is unchanged. In the PostgreSQL catalogue
  its name is lower-case (`uq_fin_journal_entry_event_ref`) because it was created unquoted.
- P3.1 keeps FIN's lookup onboarding idempotent, so it tolerates the rows BLOCK 8 may already have
  written.
- Override: move the per-type pairing into CHECKs that name 'CONSTANT' / 'MAPPING' /
  'BUSINESS_FIELD' if the lookup-in-MDL DEFAULT is dropped. Otherwise use a full UNIQUE instead of
  the partial index if hard delete ever replaces deactivation, which the DEFAULT forbids.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-029.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-029 — The v2 backend plan is restated in full, and the v1 blocks are brought to the current P3.1 template

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : REQ-FIN-001, REQ-FIN-045, REQ-FIN-050, REQ-FIN-054, REQ-FIN-062, REQ-FIN-072, API-FIN-011, API-FIN-020

## Context
A delta stage should emit only what changed. Two facts make that unsafe for this plan.

1. `gov.py state` folds a delta plan by carrying a baseline block into the delta only when it is a direct child of a
   phase the delta re-emits. CS-FIN-001 changes blocks inside every SVC-API group (API-FIN-011 in CRUD, API-FIN-020 in
   INT, the new search in SEARCH) and inside two DATA-DOM groups. A group re-emitted with only its v2 blocks would lose
   every v1 block in it from the folded state. Nothing outside a marker is carried at all — the index, the DB Alignment
   Manifest, the Error Catalog and the self-check would vanish.
2. The v1 plan passed its gate (2026-09-10) before the contracts that now check the P3.1 template existed. Read against
   today's checks it lacks an `Entity` line on 29 of 37 endpoint blocks, cites almost no DBF on its Request and
   Orchestration lines (72 `required-writer` findings), has no bootstrap section, and names a PK generation
   (`GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`) that migration V22 never built and that the v2 db-script corrects to per-table
   sequences. It also cites three wrong DBF ids: the remainder marker as DBF-FIN-103 (a rule line's amountSourceTypeCode)
   and as DBF-FIN-141 (an allocation target's lineNo), instead of DBF-FIN-107 and DBF-FIN-146. A v2 gate reads the whole
   folded plan, so this debt would block it whatever the delta did.

## Decision
- The v2 plan re-emits every phase. Records it restates unchanged — the v1 query definitions — are byte-identical to
  v1. XM-FIN-002 is left for the fold to carry.
- Every v1 endpoint block keeps its v1 text and gains three lines: `Entity` (the entity and the operation it answers),
  DBF ids on its `Request` and `Orchestration` lines (what it writes), and `Concurrency`. Where the v1 behaviour has an
  unguarded race, the Concurrency line records it as v1-as-built and does not change it. Every v1 entity block is
  rewritten to the R2 form: sequence name in BINDINGS, an OPERATIONS line, rules as a list.
- The three wrong DBF citations are corrected, in the blocks and in the Error Catalog row FIN-422-REMAINDER-MARKER.
- Every re-emitted block that differs from v1 is listed MODIFIED in the version's change manifest.

## Consequences
- No endpoint, query, rule or response changes behaviour through this ADR. Only API-FIN-011, API-FIN-020 and the
  queries QR-FIN-015, QR-FIN-025 and QR-FIN-026 change in substance, and that is CS-FIN-001's scope.
- The change manifest lists every v1 API and entity block as MODIFIED. A downstream stage that re-runs by modified id
  will revisit them. That is the cost of making the plan complete.
- The fold's one-level carry is a tool limitation. It is reported with this run and not changed here.
- Override: emit only the CS-FIN-001 blocks, once the fold carries the grandchildren of a re-emitted phase, and accept
  the inherited findings on the v1 blocks.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-030.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-030 — v2 error codes, and a uniqueness refusal answered as the business error it stands for

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : REQ-FIN-048, REQ-FIN-049, REQ-FIN-051, REQ-FIN-053, REQ-FIN-056, REQ-FIN-057, REQ-FIN-059, REQ-FIN-060, REQ-FIN-061, REQ-FIN-064, REQ-FIN-065, REQ-FIN-069, REQ-FIN-072, REQ-FIN-074, RULE-FIN-004, RULE-FIN-018, RULE-FIN-019, RULE-FIN-020, RULE-FIN-021, RULE-FIN-022, RULE-FIN-023, RULE-FIN-024, RULE-FIN-025, RULE-FIN-026, RULE-FIN-027, RULE-FIN-028, API-FIN-011, API-FIN-020, API-FIN-039, API-FIN-040, API-FIN-041

## Context
ADR-FIN-027 (P1) settled which v2 rejections are distinct errors and left the code strings to this stage. Three
more choices it did not cover have to be made here.
1. RULE-FIN-004 (MODIFIED) and RULE-FIN-022 each need a store's uniqueness refusal answered as their own error. The
   delivered platform forbids a service to catch `DataIntegrityViolationException`, and v1 therefore let such a
   refusal surface as a generic error.
2. On the event path, a date that no period covers used to answer the shared pipeline's FIN-404-PERIOD. RULE-FIN-028
   requires a distinct configuration error, never the retryable period-not-open code.
3. Updating or deactivating an unknown account mapping needs a not-found code.

## Decision
1. **Codes**, in the house format `FIN-{http}[-{SLUG}]`:
   FIN-422-UNSUPPORTED-DERIVATION (RULE-FIN-018), FIN-422-DERIVATION-SPEC (RULE-FIN-019), FIN-422-UNMAPPED-VALUE
   (RULE-FIN-020), FIN-422-MISSING-BUSINESS-FIELD (RULE-FIN-021), FIN-409-MAPPING-DUP (RULE-FIN-022),
   FIN-422-MAPPED-ACCOUNT-INELIGIBLE (RULE-FIN-023), FIN-422-INVALID-PAYMENT-METHOD (RULE-FIN-024),
   FIN-422-DIMENSION-TAG-DUP (RULE-FIN-025), FIN-422-DIMENSION-TAG-SOURCE (RULE-FIN-026),
   FIN-422-UNRESOLVED-DIMENSION-VALUE (RULE-FIN-027), FIN-422-NO-DEFINED-PERIOD (RULE-FIN-028), and
   FIN-404-ACCOUNT-MAPPING (PLATFORM-STD). A request that is well-formed but refused by a rule is 422; a clash with an
   existing row is 409, as FIN's other `…-DUP` codes are. FIN-409-DUPLICATE-EVENT and FIN-409-PERIOD-NOT-OPEN are kept
   verbatim (ADR-FIN-027). FIN-422-MAPPING-UNSUPPORTED is struck.
2. **Store refusals.** FIN gains one module-wide `FinPersistenceRefusalAdvisor`, placed like the delivered
   `FinForbiddenAdvisor`: one `DefaultPointcutAdvisor` over `com.erp.fin.service.*`, outside the transaction advisor,
   never a catch in a service and never a feature `@ControllerAdvice`. It maps a refusal by constraint name through a
   fixed registry — UQ_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRY_EVENT_REF → FIN-409-DUPLICATE-EVENT, UQ_FIN_ACCOUNT_MAPPING_ACTIVE_KEY →
   FIN-409-MAPPING-DUP — and re-throws any other refusal unchanged. The two inserts are flushed immediately, so the
   refusal happens inside the call.
3. **Period on the event path.** API-FIN-020 resolves the period that covers the event date itself (QR-FIN-059), before
   the shared pipeline. None → FIN-422-NO-DEFINED-PERIOD. Found but not OPEN → FIN-409-PERIOD-NOT-OPEN, at post.
   FIN-404-PERIOD stays the answer of API-FIN-014 and API-FIN-017, whose behaviour v2 does not change.

## Consequences
- The consumer can tell the three classes apart by code alone (DOC phase): acknowledge, wait and retry, or fail.
- Registering further v1 constraints with the advisor would turn v1's generic-error races into their `…-DUP` codes
  (UQ_FIN_ACCOUNT_CODE, UQ_FIN_DIMENSION_CODE, UQ_FIN_DIMENSION_VALUE_DIM_CODE, UQ_FIN_EVENT_TYPE_RULE_CODE,
  UQ_FIN_FISCAL_YEAR_CODE). Each would be a one-line extension. It is not taken here, because no v2 requirement asks
  for it; each endpoint's Concurrency line records the gap.
- Override: fold FIN-422-MISSING-BUSINESS-FIELD into FIN-422-UNMAPPED-VALUE (ADR-FIN-027's stated override). Or answer a
  store refusal from a platform-wide handler instead of a FIN advisor — that is a platform decision.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-031.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-031 — Event business fields travel in the existing `fields` map; the mapping search joins the account

Module  : FIN     Version : v2     Stage raised : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)
Status  : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
traces  : REQ-FIN-047, REQ-FIN-050, REQ-FIN-051, REQ-FIN-055, REQ-FIN-063, REQ-FIN-068, API-FIN-020, API-FIN-038, QR-FIN-050

## Context
1. ADR-FIN-013 names each business fact by a FIN_EVENT_BUSINESS_FIELD code, but no upstream artifact says where in the
   event request the value travels. The published `EventEntryBuildRequest` (api-docs-fin.md) already has a `fields`
   object of named string values. The unimplemented DIRECT mode used it to carry account codes, and nothing else reads it.
2. SCR-REQ-FIN-013 §B2 shows each mapping with its account's code and bilingual name. ENT-FIN-015 stores only the
   account's id (ADR-FIN-024). The engine's join governance requires an ADR for any join that fetches parent data.

## Decision
1. A business field's value is `fields[<FIN_EVENT_BUSINESS_FIELD code>]`, for example `fields.PAYMENT_METHOD`. If the key
   is absent or blank, the field is missing (RULE-FIN-021). No request field is added, and the key set grows as MDL data.
   Nothing else in `fields` is read by the rules engine, so an account code sent there is ignored (REQ-FIN-047).
2. QR-FIN-050 joins FIN_ACCOUNT on the mapping's account id and returns the account's code, nameAr and nameEn with each
   row. This is an intra-module, read-only projection. No lookup label is joined.

## Consequences
- The event contract stays additive: the published request shape is unchanged.
- The mapping screen needs no second call per row to label an account.
- Override: add a dedicated `businessFields` object to the request if a separate namespace is preferred. That would be a
  breaking change to the published request, so it would need a new ADR.

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-FIN-037 — Event business facts are named by their FIN_EVENT_BUSINESS_FIELD code inside the event's `fields` map; RULE-FIN-008's wording is corrected to remove the "may" ambiguity
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : pass-1 revise        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : merge-review-notes
Decided     : 2026-09-23

## Decision
The v2 SRS's ACs for API-FIN-020's MAPPING-derived accounts and BUSINESS_FIELD-sourced dimension
tags are re-emitted so every business fact a test builds is carried as
`fields.<FIN_EVENT_BUSINESS_FIELD code>` (e.g. `fields.PAYMENT_METHOD = "CHEQUE"`,
`fields.BRANCH_CODE = "BR-07"`, `fields.EXPENSE_TYPE_CODE = "RENT"`), matching the carrier
ADR-FIN-031 and API-FIN-020 already implement. A sentence is added to A2's general notes making
that carrier explicit at the module level. Separately, RULE-FIN-008 is re-emitted (MODIFIED, wording
only) replacing "that close may only run once every period of the year is Hard Closed" with "that
close runs only after every period of the year is Hard Closed" — no behaviour change.

## Why
The v2 SRS ACs (AC-FIN-047, AC-FIN-050…053, AC-FIN-067, AC-FIN-068, AC-FIN-071…074) previously named
the business fact as a bare field (`paymentMethod`, `branchCode`, `expenseTypeCode`). A test built
from those ACs as written would submit a payload the implementation does not recognize and would get
`FIN-422-MISSING-BUSINESS-FIELD` instead of the intended posting, contradicting ADR-FIN-031 and the
backend execution plan. RULE-FIN-008's "may" reads as permissive/optional rather than as the
temporal gate it is (C5.13).

## Consequence
No behaviour changes. Every affected AC's Given/When lines are corrected; RULE-FIN-008's Statement
text changes with no change to Data source, Message or enforcement.

Source : merge-review-notes gate pass-1, findings G1 and G9
Traces : REQ-FIN-047, REQ-FIN-050, REQ-FIN-051, REQ-FIN-063, REQ-FIN-066, REQ-FIN-068, REQ-FIN-069, REQ-FIN-020, REQ-FIN-073

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-038.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-038 — ERP-1's master entity_defaults are recorded as adapted for ENT-FIN-007 FiscalYear and ENT-FIN-008 FiscalPeriod, matching the adaptation v2 already states for ENT-FIN-015/016
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : pass-1 revise        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : merge-review-notes
Decided     : 2026-09-23

## Decision
SRS A3's preamble now records, for FiscalYear and FiscalPeriod, the same kind of adaptation of the
master `entity_defaults` that v2 already records for the two new config entities: FiscalYear's
`code` is its own bilingual-free label, so it carries no separate `nameAr`/`nameEn`; FiscalPeriod's
natural key is `periodNo` together with its `fiscalYearId`, and its lifecycle state lives in
`statusCode` (PERIOD_STATE), not in a master `isActiveFl`. No column is added, removed or retyped;
this is a documentation adaptation, not a schema change.

## Why
ERP-1 is evaluated on the whole folded P1 state, v1 included. ENT-FIN-007 has no `nameAr`/`nameEn`
and ENT-FIN-008 has no `code` and no `isActiveFl` — both pre-existing v1 facts. Left unexplained,
that reads as ERP-1 failing on two master entities. The adaptation the v2 preamble already
performs for ENT-FIN-015/016 is the correct treatment for these two as well: the profile's
`entity_defaults` are defaults, adaptable per entity where the entity's own key and lifecycle
already carry that meaning.

## Consequence
ERP-1 passes on the corrected reading. No DDL, no DBF change, no API change.

Source : merge-review-notes gate pass-1, finding G4
Traces : ENT-FIN-007, ENT-FIN-008

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-039.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-039 — AccountMapping.businessValue matches by exact code, trimmed on save and on event read, for every business field, not PAYMENT_METHOD alone
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : pass-1 revise        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : merge-review-notes
Decided     : 2026-09-23

## Decision
ENT-FIN-015.businessValue's field note now states the matching rule explicitly: compared by exact
code, with leading and trailing blanks trimmed both when the mapping is saved and when the event's
field value is read at build time (API-FIN-020). The trim applies uniformly, including to a
non-PAYMENT_METHOD business field such as EXPENSE_TYPE_CODE, which is otherwise stored and matched
as-is.

## Why
QR-FIN-052 and QR-FIN-055 already say "three key columns EXACT" and ADR-FIN-026 sets the identical
rule for dimension values, so exact matching was always the intended behaviour; the SRS simply never
stated it. Without the trim, a stray leading/trailing space typed by an administrator on save, or
present in the host system's event payload, silently produces a mapping that never resolves — the
event is rejected with FIN-422-UNMAPPED-VALUE for a fact that a human would call a match.

## Consequence
No schema change (businessValue stays VARCHAR(100), stored and compared as a plain string). The
comparison and the trim are application-layer behaviour in `AccountMappingDomain` (save) and
`EventEntryService` (build-time read of `fields[...]`), consistent with how every other lookup-backed
FIN comparison already works.

Source : merge-review-notes gate pass-1, finding G5 (downgraded from a prior round's MAJOR to MINOR)
Traces : ENT-FIN-015.businessValue, RULE-FIN-020, QR-FIN-052, QR-FIN-055

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-040.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-040 — Overlapping fiscal years stay a v1 defect; CS-FIN-001 does not undertake the fix
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : pass-1 revise        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : merge-review-notes (original) · operator (revised at the pass-1 escalation)
Decided     : 2026-09-23

## Decision
FIN does not stop two fiscal years from being created with overlapping date spans, and **v2 does not
change that**. The overlap rule, the `FIN-409-YEAR-OVERLAP` code, the `btree_gist` EXCLUDE constraint
and the pre-check query this ADR first proposed are withdrawn from this change set. The defect is
recorded as v1 debt for its own change set, alongside the other v1 gaps the pass-1 gate surfaced.

## Why
The gate's first review asked what backs QR-FIN-059's implicit "at most one period covers a date"
assumption. The answer — nothing does — is correct and worth fixing. But the fix is not this change
set's.

CS-FIN-001 is four deltas on the accounting FIN derives from a business event: account mapping,
dimension tags on rule-driven lines, the duplicate-event answer and the closed-period code. Fiscal
year creation is none of them. `API-FIN-023` is a v1 endpoint that v2 does not otherwise touch, and
the proposed fix reached across three stages — a `RULE` that P1 must mint, an extension and an
EXCLUDE constraint that P2 must create, a query and an error code in P3.1.

Taking it inside a revise produced exactly the incoherence the gate then reported: `RULE-FIN-029`
minted in P3.1 though `RULE` is P1's to own, and a constraint the plan called "the guarantee" that
`db-script` never created. A change set that quietly grows to cover what a reviewer noticed in
passing is how scope stops meaning anything.

## Consequence
- No new error code, no new store constraint, no new rule and no new query in v2.
- QR-FIN-059 keeps the v1 behaviour it has: zero rows answer `FIN-422-NO-DEFINED-PERIOD`. Its Null
  handling line now says outright that more than one row is possible and what happens then, so the
  defect is stated in the plan a reader actually reads, not only here.
- The overlap defect is recorded as consumer feedback against FIN, to be scheduled with the other
  v1 items waived at this gate.

Source : merge-review-notes gate pass-1 finding G2; pass-1 gate escalation finding G2
Traces : API-FIN-023, QR-FIN-059

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-041.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-041 — Named pessimistic-write guards close the concurrency gaps ADR-FIN-029 carried forward on API-FIN-014, API-FIN-024/025/026 and API-FIN-027
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : pass-1 revise        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : merge-review-notes
Decided     : 2026-09-23

## Decision
Four Concurrency lines, restated by ADR-FIN-029 as carrying no guard, now name one:
- **API-FIN-027 (run year-end close)** — the fiscal year row is loaded `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` before
  the OPEN-status check (the same row the docNo allocation already locks later in the same method;
  the lock is simply taken at the top of the transaction instead of only at doc-numbering time).
- **API-FIN-014 (run template)** — the template row is loaded `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` before
  `nextRunDate` is read, so two concurrent runs of one template serialize instead of both reading
  the same predecessor date and both posting.
- **API-FIN-024 / API-FIN-025 / API-FIN-026 (period open / soft-close / hard-close)** — the period
  row is loaded `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` before the current-status check, so two concurrent transitions
  on one period serialize instead of racing last-writer-wins.

## Why
ADR-FIN-029 restated these five blocks unchanged and marked them MODIFIED-in-annotation-only, but
their own Concurrency lines say plainly that no guard exists. Two concurrent year-end closes can
both pass the OPEN check and each post a CLOSING/OPENING pair, corrupting Retained Earnings; two
concurrent runs of a recurring template can double-post; and two concurrent period transitions can
leave the period in whichever state applied last. "v1 as built, unchanged" is not a fix for a defect
that corrupts financial state, and CS-FIN-001 is additive — carrying a correctness gap forward
because touching it is out of the additive change's nominal scope is not an acceptable trade against
a doubled closing entry.

## Consequence
No entity, no DTO and no endpoint contract changes. Each affected service method's load step
changes from a plain `findById` to a `findById` under `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` (Spring Data:
`@Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)` on the repository finder, or the JPA
`EntityManager.find(..., LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)` equivalent). The five Concurrency lines in
the backend execution plan are rewritten to name the guard instead of stating its absence.

Source : merge-review-notes gate pass-1, finding G3
Traces : API-FIN-014, API-FIN-024, API-FIN-025, API-FIN-026, API-FIN-027, ADR-FIN-029

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-042.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-042 — Two v1 read-decide-write races are recorded, not closed, by CS-FIN-001
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : operator (pass-1 gate escalation)
Decided     : 2026-09-23

## Decision
Two concurrency defects in v1 endpoints that v2 does not otherwise touch are stated here and left
unchanged in this change set:

1. **API-FIN-017 (run an allocation rule)** reads the source balance (QR-FIN-022, QR-FIN-043) and
   posts an entry for that amount with no guard. Two concurrent runs of one rule both read the same
   balance and both post, so a source of 1,000.00 can end at −1,000.00.
2. **API-FIN-003 (update account)** decides RULE-FIN-001 over the child set QR-FIN-006 reads, which
   a concurrent **API-FIN-002 (create account)** can extend; API-FIN-002 also flips the named
   parent's `isLeafFl` without a lock. The result can be an account that is both leaf and parent — a
   postable rollup that RULE-FIN-007 then accepts.

## Why
Both are real, and both are v1. CS-FIN-001 is four deltas on the accounting FIN derives from a
business event; allocation runs and account-tree maintenance are neither. The pass-1 revise already
placed `PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` guards on the endpoints v2 does touch (API-FIN-014, API-FIN-024,
API-FIN-025, API-FIN-026, API-FIN-027, ADR-FIN-041); extending that sweep to the rest of v1 would
make this change set a concurrency audit of the module.

The second defect is the more serious of the two, because a both-leaf-and-parent account is a state
the chart's own invariant says cannot exist, and RULE-FIN-007 — which v2 leans on for every mapped
account — trusts that invariant. v2 does not make it worse: it adds no path that creates accounts.

## Consequence
- Neither endpoint changes in v2. The Concurrency line of API-FIN-017, API-FIN-002 and API-FIN-003
  states its race, so a reader of the plan alone finds it without this ADR.
- Both are to be scheduled with the other v1 debt waived at the pass-1 gate, and the second should
  lead that list.
- If either is fixed before the legacy-accounting cutover, the fix is a v1 change set, not a v2 one.

Source : pass-1 gate escalation finding G3
Traces : API-FIN-002, API-FIN-003, API-FIN-017, RULE-FIN-001, RULE-FIN-007

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-FIN-045 — ADR-FIN-040 exists only in P3.1. RULE-FIN-029 was minted by P3.1, and no SRS rule, REQ, AC or registry-srs row backs it. The db-script creates no EXCL_FIN_FISCAL_YEAR_DATERANGE and no btree_gist extension, even though API-FIN-023 names that constraint as its guarantee. The CORE advisor registry still lists two constraints. Round 1's claim that this was "all present and consistent" is overturned.
