# ADR-FIN-060 — The fetched api-docs publish FIN's v1 as-built surface only: CS-FIN-001's account-mapping endpoints and the v2 rule-line request are not published, so SCR-FIN-013 has no endpoint to bind
Status      : SUPERSEDED by ADR-FIN-064 (was BLOCKED, 2026-09-23)
Stage       : P3.2        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : analysis
Decided     : 2026-09-23
traces      : REQ-FIN-048, REQ-FIN-049, REQ-FIN-054, REQ-FIN-055, REQ-FIN-056, REQ-FIN-057, REQ-FIN-058, REQ-FIN-059, REQ-FIN-060, REQ-FIN-061, REQ-FIN-062, REQ-FIN-064, REQ-FIN-065, SCR-FIN-003, SCR-FIN-013

## Context

The frontend plan binds to the **real** API surface, `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md`, published by the
backend repo after implementation. The engine names it the only source for endpoint shape (P3.2 engine §0, §3.0).
The copy fetched for this run is from backend commit `7706fd851d91a04faf7edc8c8924de14fa52820b`,
fetched at 2026-09-23T12:00:56Z. It describes the v1 as-built backend. Measured against the approved v2 SRS and
the P3.1 v2 registry, it lacks the following:

| # | What CS-FIN-001 needs on a screen | What the fetched api-docs publish |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account-mapping search, create, change-account and deactivate (SCR-REQ-FIN-013 §B5; REQ-FIN-054…061). P3.1 declares them as four endpoints under `/api/v1/fin/account-mappings`. | No `account-mappings` endpoint of any kind. |
| 2 | A rule line that names its business field and carries its dimension tags (REQ-FIN-049, REQ-FIN-062; RULE-FIN-019 says a MAPPING line carries **no** account code). | API-FIN-011 publishes `RuleLineCreateRequest` without a business-field member or a tag array, and makes `accountDerivationValue` **required** on every line. |
| 3 | The rule's Detail pane shows a line's business field and tags. | `RuleLineResponse` and `EventTypeRuleResponse` carry neither. |
| 4 | The v2 rejections a user can meet on these two screens: RULE-FIN-018, 019, 022, 023, 024, 025 and 026. | The Known Error Codes table carries none of the twelve v2 codes. It still publishes `FIN-422-MAPPING-UNSUPPORTED`, which P3.1 v2 retires. |

Engine §3.0 settles how this is classified: "every REQ that needs an endpoint has one (missing/renamed → ADR —
naming diffs continue, **a missing core operation is breaking**)". Account-mapping maintenance is CS-FIN-001's
acceptance 3 and the whole purpose of SCR-REQ-FIN-013, so it is a core operation. Row 2 also contradicts an
upstream artifact outright: the published request cannot express a MAPPING line as RULE-FIN-019 defines one.

## Decision

The stage stops, and this ADR is BLOCKED.

The four stage artifacts are still written in full. The design can then be reviewed at the human decision
point, and the re-run needs no new design work:

- **Part A stands whole.** The flow diagram, the ui-ux-spec, SCR-FIN-013 and UXD-FIN-013…015 depend only on the
  SRS and the PRD (P3.2 engine §2).
- **Part B binds only what is published.** Every published endpoint is cited by its published id, or by
  its published verb and path where it has no id (ADR-FIN-061). Every binding owned by the unpublished surface is
  written `PENDING ADR-FIN-060`. No API id, DTO member name, length limit or catalog code is taken from the
  backend plan's contract draft into a binding. Where the plan names a v2 catalog code, it names it only as
  "P3.1 catalogue, not yet published".

## Consequences

To unblock, in this order:
1. Implement the FIN v2 backend package (`backend/modules/FIN/packages/v2/backend-execution`), then regenerate
   and publish `backend/modules/FIN/api-docs`.
2. Run `gov.py fetch-inputs` for FIN v2, so `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` describes the v2 surface.
3. Re-run P3.2 on FIN v2. Each `PENDING ADR-FIN-060` becomes the published id, DTO and catalog code. The
   path-only citations of ADR-FIN-061 become ids wherever the regenerated api-docs carry them. The re-run
   raises the ADR that supersedes this one.

`gate:pass-2` must not open on this version of the plan. Nothing in this ADR is the frontend's to decide.
The missing surface is the backend's publication, and the frontend design already waits on it.

## Superseded (2026-09-24)

The backend published CS-FIN-001's surface, and the re-fetched api-docs (backend commit `4cbe044…`) carry
all four gaps above. The re-run of P3.2 bound every `PENDING ADR-FIN-060` to its published id, DTO and code.
See ADR-FIN-064. This ADR no longer stops the stage.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-061.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-061 — Served endpoints that the api-docs publish without a contract id are cited by verb and path; the v1 plan's provisional API-FIN-038 is withdrawn
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.2        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : analysis
Decided     : 2026-09-23
traces      : REQ-FIN-005, REQ-FIN-007, REQ-FIN-022, REQ-FIN-025, REQ-FIN-031, SCR-FIN-002, SCR-FIN-003, SCR-FIN-004, SCR-FIN-005, SCR-FIN-006, SCR-FIN-007

## Context

The catalog in `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` gives a contract id to 32 of the 38 served endpoints (API-FIN-001…032).
Its drift table reports the other six as "undeclared":

| Published endpoint | P3.1 v2 registry id | v1 frontend plan cited it as |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-periods/search` | API-FIN-033 | API-FIN-033 (ADR-FIN-002 binding annex) |
| `PUT /api/v1/fin/event-rules/{id}/deactivate` | API-FIN-034 | API-FIN-034 (annex) |
| `PUT /api/v1/fin/dimensions/values/{id}/deactivate` | API-FIN-035 | API-FIN-035 (annex) |
| `PUT /api/v1/fin/recurring-templates/{id}/deactivate` | API-FIN-036 | API-FIN-036 (annex) |
| `PUT /api/v1/fin/allocation-rules/{id}/deactivate` | API-FIN-037 | API-FIN-037 (annex) |
| `POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/search` | **none** | API-FIN-038, a provisional id (ADR-FIN-006) |

Two facts changed after v1:
- `gov.py analyze` C9.5 now accepts only ids that the **fetched api-docs** define. The companion binding annex is
  not an input it reads. As a result, the folded v1 plan fails six CRITICAL clauses before this stage writes anything.
- P3.1 v2 has minted **API-FIN-038 for the account-mapping search**. The v1 plan's provisional API-FIN-038 now
  names a different endpoint.

## Decision

The frontend plan cites each of these six endpoints by its published verb and path, and by no id that the api-docs do not
carry. All six are published and served, and the frontend uses all six exactly as in v1. The P3.1 ids for the first five
are kept in `registry-exec-fe-fin.md` (API COVERAGE) as a cross-reference only.

The fiscal-year search stays the source of SCR-FIN-007's Master pane and of the required `fiscalYearId`
inputs of SCR-FIN-010 and SCR-FIN-011. No id exists for it in the api-docs or in P3.1's registry. That is a gap in
P3.1's API REGISTRY (a served endpoint with no contract id), recorded here for P3.1. The frontend does not mint an id,
because it owns no `API-*`.

This ADR supersedes two things:
- ADR-FIN-002's binding annex, as a source of API ids.
- The sentence of ADR-FIN-006 that names the fiscal-year search "API-FIN-038". The rest of ADR-FIN-006 stands.

## Consequences

- The change is non-breaking. Only the naming differs, and every operation is published (engine §3.0, "naming diffs
  continue").
- When regenerated api-docs carry these ids, the path citations become ids in the same re-run that ADR-FIN-060
  requires. The binding does not change.
- P3.1 should number `POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/search` in its next delta.

## Narrowed (2026-09-24, ADR-FIN-064)

The republished api-docs number the first five endpoints of the table above as API-FIN-033 … API-FIN-037,
and the frontend plan now cites them by id. Only `POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/search` is still published
without a contract id, so it alone is still cited by verb and path.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-062.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-062 — Engine-rule lines are added one per submit from the Detail pane, never batched behind the rule's save
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.2        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : analysis
Decided     : 2026-09-23
traces      : REQ-FIN-007, REQ-FIN-008, REQ-FIN-049, REQ-FIN-062, SCR-FIN-003

## Context

In v1, SCR-FIN-003's ui-ux-spec put the rule's line collection behind the rule Entry, as a summary row that opens a
second-level Drawer. It never said how many calls the Entry's single save makes.

The published surface makes that save a batch. API-FIN-010 creates a rule with no lines. API-FIN-011 adds exactly one
line per call. The SRS (SCR-REQ-FIN-003 §B4) records that a line has no update and no delete. v2 adds dimension tags
that travel inside the add-line submission and share the line's lifecycle (ADR-FIN-025).

A "save rule with N lines" would therefore be 1 + N ordered calls. If call k fails, the rule already holds lines
1…k−1, and the screen has no way to correct or remove them. This is the partial save that P3.2 engine §A.4 forbids:
"a rejected update cannot leave the record carrying children never saved with it".

## Decision

Each surface on SCR-FIN-003 creates one record and submits once:
- **Rule Entry.** Takes eventTypeCode, nameAr and nameEn. It saves the rule and nothing else.
- **Line entry.** Opened from the Detail pane of an already-saved, selected rule. It saves one line together with its
  dimension tags, which is one API-FIN-011 call. The tags are a summary row that opens a second-level editor. That
  editor returns the tag list to the line's form state and never saves.

A new rule is therefore created first and then given its lines one at a time. The RULE-FIN-003 remainder check stays
server-authoritative. The client pre-empts only what it can know, which is that no second line of the rule carries
the remainder marker.

## Consequences

- SCR-FIN-003's `Composition` line and the F2, F3 and F4 blocks follow this decision. The v1 composition, with
  lines behind the rule Entry, is superseded.
- If the backend ever publishes a rule-with-lines create in one call, this ADR is superseded, and the lines can
  return behind the rule's save as one call.
- The change is non-breaking. It narrows how the screen uses published endpoints and removes no operation.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-063.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-063 — Test generation for FIN v2: complete re-emission, the in-track denominator, cases bound to an unpublished surface, and five stale v1 cases
Status      : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
Stage       : test-gen (Test Generation, standalone)        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : test-gen
Decided     : 2026-09-23
traces      : AC-FIN-045, AC-FIN-049, AC-FIN-081, REQ-FIN-045, REQ-FIN-075, SCR-FIN-003, SCR-FIN-013

## Context

CS-FIN-001 adds thirty-seven acceptance criteria (AC-FIN-047 … AC-FIN-083), modifies AC-FIN-045,
and adds one screen (SCR-FIN-013). The test-gen engine forbids questions, so every choice below
that was not mechanical had to be settled here. ADR-FIN-009 (v1) stands unchanged: TCs derive
from ACs alone, the frontend denominator is the set of ACs a screen can exercise, and onboarding
ACs carry an empty `Exercises` binding. This ADR extends it to v2.

Five facts forced a decision.

**(a) A delta test plan cannot be a fragment.** The engine says to emit only ADDED, MODIFIED and
REMOVED cases. But `gov.py state` folds a marker plan by phase, carrying back only a phase's
missing **direct** children, which here are the SUBs `RULE-SCENARIOS` / `API-SCENARIOS` and
`UI-FLOWS` / `INT-FLOW`. A v2 SUB holding only its v2 atoms would replace the v1 SUB of the same
label, and every v1 case inside it would vanish from `_state/current-*-test-plan.md`. The profile
fixes the SUB labels, so the v2 cases cannot live in SUBs of their own. The P3.1 and P3.2 v2
plans met the same constraint and re-emitted in full (ADR-FIN-029).

**(b) The version check reads a byte-identical marker atom as re-defined.** `ids-continue`
(C12.3) keeps one baseline text per id — the heading record, the last one it reads. It then
compares every record of the new file against that text, the TC's START-marker record included,
which is a separate, one-line record. So a v1 case restated word for word is still reported as
"re-defined … but not listed as MODIFIED". In the same way, the last v1 case before a SUB whose
START `traces=` grew has a heading record that runs on to that marker, so its text differs even
though its content does not: TC-FIN-049 on the backend, TC-FIN-091 on the frontend.

**(c) Twenty-one v2 ACs have no screen.** Their When is an event arriving — the mapped account,
the resolved dimension, and every event rejection happen inside API-FIN-020, which no screen
calls (ADR-FIN-007). AC-FIN-081 asks what a published document says.

**(d) The frontend's v2 surface is designed but not callable.** SCR-FIN-013 and the v2 half of
SCR-FIN-003's Line entry are drawn in full — route, guard, facade, forms. Their calls, the v2
members of API-FIN-011 and the twelve v2 catalogue codes are not in the fetched api-docs. That is
ADR-FIN-060, BLOCKED at P3.2. The backend plan, by contrast, declares all of them.

**(e) Five v1 cases went stale without their ACs changing, and one AC changed.** AC-FIN-045 now
says fifteen lookup types. TC-FIN-044 counted twelve screens and twenty-seven actions, where v2
has thirteen and thirty. TC-FIN-008 offered DIRECT as test data, which RULE-FIN-018 now refuses.
TC-FIN-010 and TC-FIN-012 asserted 201 on the build-from-event endpoint, whose published
contract answers 200. On the frontend, TC-FIN-059, TC-FIN-060 and TC-FIN-061 described v1's
engine-rules form, which is replaced by the one-line-per-submit form of ADR-FIN-062. TC-FIN-079
said no fiscal-year search exists, which ADR-FIN-061 superseded.

## Decision

1. **Both test plans are re-emitted complete.** v1 cases that v2 leaves alone are restated
   byte-identical. v2 cases **open** each SUB, so that the last v1 case of the phase keeps its
   record text. The test-execution manifest carries no id and is regenerated in full.

2. **The change manifest lists every re-emitted v1 case as MODIFIED**: TC-FIN-001 … TC-FIN-052
   on the backend and TC-FIN-053 … TC-FIN-092 on the frontend. This is forced by (b), and it
   follows the precedent of the P3.1 plan, which lists API-FIN-001 … API-FIN-037. Each plan's
   header names the cases whose content actually changed, and the manifest carries the same
   list as a note:
   - backend: TC-FIN-008, TC-FIN-010, TC-FIN-012, TC-FIN-044, TC-FIN-045;
   - frontend: TC-FIN-059, TC-FIN-060, TC-FIN-061, TC-FIN-079.

   TC-FIN-049 and TC-FIN-091 are named separately, as record-boundary changes only.

3. **v2 ids continue the one shared sequence.** The backend track takes TC-FIN-093 …
   TC-FIN-129, one case per v2 AC in AC order (TC = AC + 46). The frontend track takes TC-FIN-130
   … TC-FIN-145, one per in-track v2 AC in AC order. No boundary, permission or extra case is
   added. No v2 AC states a numeric limit that its own case does not already test (AC-FIN-082 is
   the boundary), and none is a permission AC.

4. **The frontend denominator becomes 56 of 83.** That is v1's 40 plus the sixteen v2 ACs a
   screen can exercise: AC-FIN-048, 049, 058 … 066, 069, 070, 075, 076 and 083. The twenty-seven
   outside it are listed in the frontend header, each beside the backend case that covers it.
   Module-wide coverage is 83/83.

5. **Cases bound to the unpublished surface are written now, against the drawn screen.** These
   are TC-FIN-130 … TC-FIN-142. Each states in its Preconditions that the call it needs must be
   published (ADR-FIN-060). They assert the SRS messages character-perfect in both languages,
   and they name each code as the backend plan's catalogue does. The frontend coverage block
   counts them as waiting. This delays when they run; it narrows nothing they assert, and it is
   not a derivation blocker. Nothing on the backend track waits.

6. **AC-FIN-081 gets a document case.** TC-FIN-127 is bound to API-FIN-020's published error
   catalogue, read as a document with no call. It states that the copy fetched for P3.2 lacks
   the message and note the AC asks for, so it fails until the backend republishes.

7. **As-built v2 behaviour that no AC states gets no case**, extending ADR-FIN-009 §2:
   - the store-refusal half of FIN-409-MAPPING-DUP;
   - FIN-404-ACCOUNT-MAPPING;
   - the blank-value half of RULE-FIN-021;
   - the trimming of `businessValue` (ADR-FIN-039);
   - FIN-422-DERIVATION-SPEC. RULE-FIN-019's only AC, AC-FIN-049, is the passing case.

   Each is named in the plans' "catalog rows no TC exercises" lists.
   FIN-422-MAPPING-UNSUPPORTED is struck in v2 (ADR-FIN-027) and is treated like
   FIN-403-SOD-VIOLATION: not a gap, and not to be tested.

8. **The five stale backend cases and four stale frontend cases are modified** to their v2 truth,
   each change sourced from the v2 SRS, backend plan or frontend plan. AC-FIN-045's case follows
   the AC's own new text.

## Consequences

- Backend: 89 cases (52 + 37), AC 83/83, REQ 77/77, API 32/41. The nine endpoints without a
  case are the same nine v1 had. v1's printed 26/37 was a miscount of its own table, which
  counts 28, and v2 prints the table's figure.
- Frontend: 56 cases (40 + 16), AC 56/56 in track, SCR 13/13. Thirteen cases wait for
  ADR-FIN-060.
- The fold of `_state/current-*-test-plan.md` carries nothing from v1: every v1 child is present
  in the delta.
- Nothing in FIN's line artifacts changes. No REQ, AC, RULE, API, screen or catalogue row is
  added, removed or reworded. The gaps named in decision 7 are for P1 to close, if anyone wants
  them covered.
- A later factory fix to `ids-continue` — comparing a marker record with the baseline's marker
  record — would let a later delta list only the cases whose content changed.

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-FIN-064 — The republished api-docs carry CS-FIN-001's surface, so every binding ADR-FIN-060 left pending is bound to its published id, DTO and code; ADR-FIN-060 is superseded and ADR-FIN-061 narrows to the fiscal-year search
Status      : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
Stage       : P3.2        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : analysis
Decided     : 2026-09-24
traces      : REQ-FIN-005, REQ-FIN-007, REQ-FIN-022, REQ-FIN-025, REQ-FIN-031, REQ-FIN-048, REQ-FIN-049, REQ-FIN-054, REQ-FIN-055, REQ-FIN-056, REQ-FIN-057, REQ-FIN-058, REQ-FIN-059, REQ-FIN-060, REQ-FIN-061, REQ-FIN-062, REQ-FIN-064, REQ-FIN-065, REQ-FIN-075, SCR-FIN-002, SCR-FIN-003, SCR-FIN-004, SCR-FIN-005, SCR-FIN-006, SCR-FIN-007, SCR-FIN-013

## Context

The previous run of this stage (2026-09-23) stopped on ADR-FIN-060 (BLOCKED). The api-docs fetched then described
FIN's v1 as-built surface: no account-mapping endpoint, no v2 member on the add-rule-line request or response, none
of the v2 catalogue codes, and a contract id on only 32 of the served endpoints. ADR-FIN-060 named the way out:
implement the v2 backend, republish the api-docs, fetch them, and re-run P3.2.

That has happened. `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` was re-fetched on 2026-09-23T20:36Z from backend commit `4cbe044…`.
Measured against the four gaps ADR-FIN-060 listed:

| # | ADR-FIN-060 gap | Republished api-docs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No account-mapping endpoint | Search, create, change account and deactivate are published as API-FIN-038, API-FIN-039, API-FIN-040 and API-FIN-041, gated by the page's VIEW, CREATE and UPDATE permissions. The search response carries the mapped account's code and names. |
| 2 | Add-rule-line request cannot express a MAPPING line | API-FIN-011's request carries `accountBusinessFieldCode` and a `dimensionTags` array, and `accountDerivationValue` is no longer required. |
| 3 | Rule and line responses carry no business field or tags | Every rule and line response carries both. |
| 4 | No v2 catalogue code; the retired MAPPING-unsupported code still listed | All twelve v2 codes are published with ar/en messages. The retired code is gone. The period-not-open code is listed once, with its message and the note that the rejection clears once the period is opened (AC-FIN-081). |

The catalog also now numbers the five endpoints ADR-FIN-061 cited by path (API-FIN-033 … API-FIN-037), matching
the P3.1 v2 registry. Its drift table reports one served endpoint without a contract id:
`POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/search`, which P3.1's registry has never numbered.

## Decision

1. Every binding that read `PENDING ADR-FIN-060` is bound to the published id, DTO member and catalogue code. The
   plan cites nothing from the backend plan's contract draft.
2. ADR-FIN-060 is superseded. Its status changes from BLOCKED to SUPERSEDED. The stage no longer stops on it.
3. ADR-FIN-061 narrows. The five endpoints the api-docs now number are cited by id. Only the fiscal-year search is
   still cited by verb and path, for the reason ADR-FIN-061 gives.
4. The design does not change. Part A stood whole in the previous run. The only spec edits are the endpoint each
   screen names and two error states the republished catalogue now documents: FIN-404-DIMENSION on the dimension
   report and the not-found codes on account mappings.
5. The Line entry's Save is no longer disabled for a MAPPING or tagged line. SCR-FIN-013's calls are bound.

## Consequences

- Non-breaking. No operation, field, rule or permission is added or removed. The screens now call endpoints that
  exist.
- Every screen-facing REQ is bound to a published endpoint. The plan's UNMAPPED list is empty apart from the one
  path citation.
- The v2 test plans (ADR-FIN-063) bound some cases to the then-unpublished surface. They were written before this
  binding and should be checked against it at their next run. Test generation owns that decision, not this stage.
- P3.1 should still number `POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/search` in its next delta (ADR-FIN-061).

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-065.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-065 — The frontend's consumer feedback is answered in the plan: owned-collection screens become list + record pages hydrated by a published `<entity>Pk` search, and eight binding gaps are closed
Status      : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
Stage       : P3.2        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : analysis
Decided     : 2026-09-24
traces      : SCR-FIN-001, SCR-FIN-002, SCR-FIN-003, SCR-FIN-004, SCR-FIN-005, SCR-FIN-006, SCR-FIN-007, SCR-FIN-008, SCR-FIN-009, SCR-FIN-010, SCR-FIN-011, SCR-FIN-012, SCR-FIN-013, REQ-FIN-004, REQ-FIN-005, REQ-FIN-007, REQ-FIN-009, REQ-FIN-014, REQ-FIN-017, REQ-FIN-019, REQ-FIN-021, REQ-FIN-022, REQ-FIN-025, REQ-FIN-028, REQ-FIN-031, REQ-FIN-034, REQ-FIN-037, REQ-FIN-041, REQ-FIN-042, REQ-FIN-046, REQ-FIN-054

## Context

The frontend implementation of this plan (the mxdashboard FIN module) filed thirteen feedback records against
it, FB-1 … FB-13. The project owner has already decided the design questions they raise. This ADR records those
decisions and the plan edits that carry them. It re-opens none of them.

Every endpoint shape below was checked against `_inputs/api-docs-fin.md` as fetched for this stage. Every route
name was checked against the shipped `mxdashboard/src/App.tsx` and the feature `*RoutePaths.ts` files.

## Decision

### 1. Owned-collection screens are a list page and a record page (FB-1, FB-2, FB-7)

Owner decision, 2026-09-21. The rule sources are `erp-drawer-zustand` §11 and `ui-master-detail-records`.

Five screens hold a record that OWNS a child collection:

| Screen | Record → child collection | List | New | Record page | Cold-load read (published filter) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCR-FIN-002 | dimension → values | `/fin/dimensions` | `/fin/dimensions/new` | `/fin/dimensions/:dimensionId` | API-FIN-005, `dimensionPk EQUALS` |
| SCR-FIN-003 | rule → lines | `/fin/rules` | `/fin/rules/new` | `/fin/rules/:ruleId` | API-FIN-009, `eventTypeRulePk EQUALS` |
| SCR-FIN-004 | template → lines | `/fin/recurring-templates` | `/fin/recurring-templates/new` | `/fin/recurring-templates/:templateId` | API-FIN-012, `recurringTemplatePk EQUALS` |
| SCR-FIN-005 | allocation rule → targets | `/fin/allocation-rules` | `/fin/allocation-rules/new` | `/fin/allocation-rules/:allocationRuleId` | API-FIN-015, `allocationRulePk EQUALS` |
| SCR-FIN-007 | fiscal year → periods | `/fin/periods` | `/fin/periods/new` | `/fin/periods/:fiscalYearId` | `POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/search` (ADR-FIN-061), `fiscalYearPk EQUALS` |

The api-docs list each filter under that search's "Supported fields" as `(EQUALS, IN)`.

Each of the five screens has the same shape:
- **List page.** The whole viewport shows the list.
- **Record page.** The header form sits inline in a collapsible section with its own single submit. The child
  collection sits beneath it.
- **Child line add or edit.** A Drawer on its own search param: `?valueAction=create`, `?lineAction=create` or
  `?targetAction=create`.
- **`/new`.** Registered before `/:id`. After a save, the page moves to the record page, using the id from the
  CREATE RESPONSE.

Two screens have a published child write addressed by the parent's id: SCR-FIN-002 (API-FIN-007) and SCR-FIN-003
(API-FIN-011). On their `/new` pages the child section is locked and says why.

Two screens create the parent and its children in one call: SCR-FIN-004 (API-FIN-013) and SCR-FIN-005
(API-FIN-016). On their `/new` pages the children are composed in the line Drawer, and the one create sends them.
On their record pages the children are read-only, because no child write is published (ADR-FIN-006).

SCR-FIN-007's periods are generated by the year's create. On its record page they carry the transition row
actions.

**The cold-load read.** The record page hydrates on a cold deep link through the screen's PUBLISHED search, with
one filter, `<entity>Pk EQUALS <id>`, at page 0 and size 1. The search response carries the full aggregate. The
read is one F2 record hook per screen, under that screen's existing query-key root, so every invalidation the
plan already declares refreshes it. A zero-row answer renders an honest "not found" notice with a way back to the
list, never an empty form.

**ADR-FIN-006 narrows.** Its "no by-id read" stands for ENDPOINTS: no by-id endpoint is invented. A filtered
search is the record read.

**Not affected.** SCR-FIN-001 owns no child collection (a parent account is a reference, not an owned line; see
the ownership test in `ui-master-detail-records` §5), so it keeps Search + Entry Drawer. SCR-FIN-013 is a flat
record and keeps its Drawer too. SCR-FIN-006 already had `/new` and `/:id`. The report screens are unaffected
(ADR-FIN-003).

The ALIGN-FE operations-coverage table now names the record route for every write that lives on it, and names
the second role of the five searches.

### 2. SCR-FIN-006's fiscal-year select (FB-3)

The manual-entry form's year select is bound to the fiscal-year option read, `POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/search`,
which is still cited by path (ADR-FIN-061). F2-SCR-FIN-006-FACADE now publishes the year options. Components still
read nothing except the facade.

The period select is narrowed client-side by `period.fiscalYearId`. The server's FIN-400-PERIOD-NOT-IN-YEAR and
FIN-400-DOCDATE-OUTSIDE-PERIOD remain the authority (RULE-FIN-017).

### 3. Balance sheet to trial balance drill-down (FB-4)

API-FIN-029 publishes exactly two query parameters, `periodId` and `accountTypeCode`. API-FIN-030 returns no
period. The drill therefore carries the row GROUP's `accountTypeCode` only, to
`/fin/reports/trial-balance?accountTypeCode=<code>`. It carries no account and no period. The flow diagram and
SCR-FIN-010's navigation say so.

The income-statement drill-down claimed the same two carriers and has the same defect: API-FIN-031 returns a
period range, while the trial balance takes one period. It is corrected the same way, to the group's
`accountTypeCode` only.

### 4. Income statement bounds (FB-5)

The api-docs publish `fromPeriodId` and `toPeriodId` on API-FIN-031 as independently optional, with no
cross-field rule. The filter schema and F2-SCR-FIN-011-FACADE send each bound that is set, on its own. They never
couple the two and never drop a half-specified range. An open-ended range ("from period 3") is a legal request.

### 5. Action affordances (FB-6, FB-12)

ADR-FIN-005 stands. There is no client-side action-level gating. No published endpoint carries the caller's
action-level permissions: the SEC effective menu (ADR-FIN-005) carries page codes only.

Every affordance renders for a caller who holds the screen. That includes CREATE, UPDATE, run, reverse, reopen,
hard-close and year-end-close. FIN-403-FORBIDDEN is the authority, and it is shown as the localized catalogue
message on the screen.

Removed from the plan:
- SEC-FE's "hidden without the grant" wording;
- the F4 Guard lines that made an affordance need CREATE, UPDATE or the Close-approve presence flag;
- the SCREEN-INIT rows that claimed an action-level permission read.

A data-state precondition is also left to the server. The year-end close renders enabled and shows a readiness
hint while periods are still open, and the server's FIN-409-PERIODS-NOT-CLOSED decides. The same holds for a
reopen after a hard close: FIN-409-NOT-REOPENABLE decides.

RULE-FIN-015's separation of duty is demonstrated by the server's 403, not by the screen. TC-FIN-082 step 2 and
TC-FIN-086 step 2 assert the gate this ADR removes. Test generation should align them at its next run. This
stage does not own them.

### 6. Nullable response fields (FB-8)

This is a plan-wide F1 rule. Every response field the api-docs mark as not required, or describe as null in some
case, is typed `T | null`, because the wire sends JSON `null`. It is never typed `?: T`. Presence tests use
`== null` / `!= null`, never `=== undefined`.

The rule is stated in PHASE F1's conventions and repeated in F1-SCR-FIN-003, F1-SCR-FIN-006 and F1-SCR-FIN-013.
The defect it prevents was live: a false "reversal" notice rendered on every entry, and the Reverse action was
permanently disabled.

### 7. Option reads (FB-13)

Every option read sends page 0 and size 200, the api-docs' maximum. Every option consumer discloses `hasMore`
(`totalElements > options.length`) when the set is capped, and it never truncates silently. That covers the
picker Drawers and also every plain `<select>`, including:
- the fiscal-year selects of SCR-FIN-010 and SCR-FIN-011;
- the year and period selects of SCR-FIN-006;
- SCR-FIN-013's selects.

Whether a required-filter select should become a searchable picker once its domain is unbounded is left open.
Disclosure is the rule today.

### 8. Event-rule business 409s (FB-10)

The republished api-docs bind FIN-409-RULE-DUP to API-FIN-010 and FIN-409-REMAINDER-COUNT to API-FIN-011, each
in that endpoint's Business Responses. SCR-FIN-003 binds both, inline:
- FIN-409-RULE-DUP on the rule Entry's eventTypeCode, with the message that an active rule already exists for the
  event type;
- FIN-409-REMAINDER-COUNT on the Line entry's remainder flag.

### 9. Journal-entry line refusals (FB-11)

FIN-409-NOT-POSTABLE-ACCOUNT and FIN-409-INVALID-DIMENSION on API-FIN-019 identify no line. `fieldErrors[].field`
carries the catalogue code, with no line index, line number, account id or dimension id. The plan binds each
refusal to the lines pane's refusal slot, announced exactly once. It never binds it to a guessed line.

**Known limitation.** AC-FIN-019 (offending line) and AC-FIN-021 (offending line and dimension) cannot be asserted
at line granularity until the backend publishes the offending line in `fieldErrors[].field`, and the dimension
code in `message` for FIN-409-INVALID-DIMENSION. This is a backend follow-up for P3.1's next delta.

### Out of scope: three app defects (FB-9)

FB-9 reports three implementation defects:
- a duplicate success toast on a heavy rule record;
- a stale previous entry rendered while record-to-record navigation loads;
- the FilterDrawer staying open over the grid it filtered.

None is a plan defect, and the plan already forbids each outcome. They are handed to the frontend's defect list.

## Consequences

- Non-breaking. No operation, field, rule, permission or endpoint is added or removed. The record read is a
  published search with a published filter.
- ADR-FIN-006 is narrowed, not superseded. It carries a note that points here.
- Changed: ui-ux-spec (SCR-FIN-002 … 007, 010, 011 and 013), flow diagram (the five master-detail flows and the
  two statement drill-downs), frontend plan (the F1 rule, the F2 record hooks and option rule, the F3 income
  bounds, the F4 routes and guards, the SEC-FE table and the ALIGN-FE route column) and the registry's ADR list.
  All of these were already MODIFIED in v2, so the change manifest's classifications do not change.
- Carried to other stages:
  - the backend follow-up on line-level refusals (§9);
  - the test-case alignment for TC-FIN-082 and TC-FIN-086 (§5);
  - P3.1 numbering the fiscal-year search (ADR-FIN-061).

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-FIN-066.md>>>
# ADR-FIN-066 — Test generation re-run for FIN v2: the cases follow the frontend plan as ADR-FIN-064 and ADR-FIN-065 revised it, and a line-level AC half the published contract cannot meet is kept and stated as failing
Status      : ACCEPTED (non-breaking)
Stage       : test-gen (Test Generation, standalone)        Module: FIN        Version: v2
Lane        : test-gen
Decided     : 2026-09-24
traces      : AC-FIN-019, AC-FIN-021, AC-FIN-034, AC-FIN-036, AC-FIN-038, AC-FIN-042, AC-FIN-046, AC-FIN-081, REQ-FIN-019, REQ-FIN-021, REQ-FIN-038, REQ-FIN-075, SCR-FIN-002, SCR-FIN-003, SCR-FIN-004, SCR-FIN-005, SCR-FIN-006, SCR-FIN-007, SCR-FIN-010, SCR-FIN-011, SCR-FIN-013

## Context

The first v2 run of this stage (ADR-FIN-063) wrote its cases against the frontend plan of
2026-09-23, whose v2 surface was then unpublished (ADR-FIN-060, BLOCKED). Since then P3.2 has been
re-run twice:

- **ADR-FIN-064.** The republished api-docs carry CS-FIN-001's surface. ADR-FIN-060 is superseded,
  and so is the period-not-open note AC-FIN-081 asks for.
- **ADR-FIN-065.** The frontend build's consumer feedback is answered in the plan:
  - the five screens that own a child collection become a list, a `/new` page and a `/:id` record
    page;
  - no action is gated on the client, so every affordance renders for a holder of the screen and
    the server's 403 is the control;
  - the two journal-entry line refusals are bound to the lines pane's single refusal slot, because
    the published error body names no line;
  - the income-statement bounds are sent independently, and the balance sheet drills to the trial
    balance by the group's account type.

ADR-FIN-064 and ADR-FIN-065 both name this stage as the owner of the case alignment. The stage's
state therefore held cases that asserted:
- a hidden close-approve affordance (TC-FIN-082, TC-FIN-086) and a year-end close enabled only
  once every period is hard-closed (TC-FIN-084);
- routes the plan no longer draws (`?line=new`, a master list selected in place);
- a journal-line refusal shown against the offending line (TC-FIN-063, TC-FIN-067, TC-FIN-069);
- an income-statement range whose bounds travel together (TC-FIN-090);
- a catalogue case that fails until the backend republishes (TC-FIN-127);
- thirteen cases waiting on ADR-FIN-060.

One fact is not mechanical. AC-FIN-019 says the rejection names the offending line, and AC-FIN-021
says it names the offending line and dimension. The published error body of API-FIN-019 names
neither. ADR-FIN-065 §9 records that as a known limitation and a backend follow-up.

## Decision

1. **Every case follows the current frontend plan.** Routes are the plan's own; preconditions name
   the permission the server checks, never an affordance the client reads; each refusal is shown
   where the plan binds it (inline, generic, the lines pane's refusal slot, or the screen's
   forbidden message).

2. **No case asserts client-side gating.** TC-FIN-082, TC-FIN-084 and TC-FIN-086 are re-derived
   from their ACs. The action renders; the server's FIN-409-PERIODS-NOT-CLOSED,
   FIN-409-NOT-REOPENABLE or FIN-403-FORBIDDEN decides, and the case asserts that message on the
   screen. The separation of duty RULE-FIN-015 requires is asserted as server-enforced only.

3. **A picker's pre-empt is observed, and then bypassed.** The account pickers of SCR-FIN-006 list
   active leaf accounts only. A case whose AC needs a rollup or deactivated account on a line
   (TC-FIN-055, TC-FIN-063, TC-FIN-067) asserts that the picker does not offer it, then submits
   past it and asserts the server's refusal. This is the rule every earlier pre-empt case follows.

4. **The line-naming half of AC-FIN-019 and AC-FIN-021 is kept, not dropped or reworded.**
   - On the frontend track, TC-FIN-067 and TC-FIN-069 assert what the screen can show: the
     message once, in the lines pane's refusal slot, bound to no line.
   - On the backend track, TC-FIN-019 and TC-FIN-021 keep the AC's Then and state that this half
     is expected to fail against the build until the backend publishes the line, and the dimension
     too for the second. That is the follow-up ADR-FIN-065 records.
   - A test plan that silently dropped the half would hide a requirement the build does not meet.
     Rewording it would restate an AC, which this engine may not do.

5. **TC-FIN-127 reads a catalogue that now holds the note** (ADR-FIN-064) and is no longer stated
   as failing.

6. **Ids, counts and the change-manifest classes do not change.** No case is added or removed, and
   no id is reassigned. Every re-emitted v1 case stays MODIFIED, for the reason ADR-FIN-063 §(b)
   gives. The manifest's NOTE rows name the cases whose content changed:
   - backend: TC-FIN-019 and TC-FIN-021 (and the ADDED case TC-FIN-127);
   - frontend: every v1 case except TC-FIN-065, TC-FIN-066, TC-FIN-075, TC-FIN-077, TC-FIN-078,
     TC-FIN-087, TC-FIN-088, TC-FIN-089 and TC-FIN-091.

## Consequences
